title: explainableCoreSupply_iff_moment: F4 supply = F5 deep moments E_r
evidence: The connection's IDENTITY half (explainableCoreSupply_iff_moment, ExplainableCoreSupply <-> uniform binomial moment Sum_c C(|A_c|, k+m+1) <= B; moment_identity_base Sum_c C(|A_c|,k)=C(n,k)) is a CORRECT in-tree axiom-clean Lean lemma. But the LOAD-BEARING claim being attacked -- that the F4 supply moment and the F5 additive deep moment E_r are 'one wall', i.e. the supply-moment crossover t* lands at the same place as the W-anomaly r* (attack_plan: 'cross-check whether the supply-moment crossover ... lands at the same t*~beta+1 as the W-anomaly r*') -- is REFUTED by exact integer probes at proper dyadic subgroups in the prize regime. Probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/C087_moment_crossover.py + C087_anomaly_proper.py. Decisive data (n=8, mu_8 proper, q=1 mod 8 prime, exact DP tuple/subset counting): the additive moment T_t (ordered tuples WITH repetition summing to 0 mod q, = the E_r content via E_r=(q*T_{2r}-n^{2r})/n) PICKS UP mod-p-only solutions as q shrinks -- T_4: 168(big q)->200(q=41)->264(q=17); T_6: 5120->5600->8240->15560 -- this is exactly the W-anomaly / BGK defect onset at q~n^t (t~beta). In contrast the SUPPLY moment Z_t (the SAME zero-sum object but as DISTINCT-element UNORDERED t-SUBSETS, which is what the tower-word cores actually count per supply_ge_towerZeroSum/tower_degenerateSets_eq) is COMPLETELY q-INDEPENDENT across the whole prize regime: Z_4=6, Z_6=4 are constant for EVERY prime including q=17 (beta=1.36) where the additive object is +57% anomalous. n=16 confirms Z_t frozen at its char-0 value (8,28,56,70) for all beta>=2.1 (q>~n^2), with deviation ONLY at degenerate q~n (beta<2). So the two crossovers are PARAMETRICALLY DIFFERENT: additive anomaly onset at q~n^t (t~beta, FIRES in prize regime), supply anomaly onset at q~n (beta~1-2, ABSENT in prize regime beta=4-5). The supply face carries NO mod-p anomaly in the prize regime -- it is a frozen char-0 combinatorial count bounded by C(n,t) -- whereas the additive face's anomaly IS the BGK defect. The 'binomial moment of the agreement spectrum' (unordered subsets, q-free, the genuine #389 supply object) and the 'additive deep moment E_r' (ordered tuples with repetition, q-weighted, the genuine BGK object) are structurally distinct objects (also differ by a strict parity gate: odd Z_t=0 for thin mu_n; T_t has no such gate), so the W-anomaly has NO combinatorial twin in the supply face and 'the two moment walls are one' is FALSE.
honest_note: The Lean identity itself (supply = degenerate-j-set count, charter quantity IS a binomial moment) is genuinely proven and not in dispute -- it correctly makes the #389 supply residual a binomial moment, which is a real reformulation. What is refuted is only the further CROSS-FACE identification of that supply moment with the additive E_r anomaly (the 'why_insightful'/'attack_plan' claim that the W-anomaly and the supply crossover are the same wall). The refutation is at proper dyadic subgroups n in {8,16,32} with multiple large prize primes (beta up to 5.0), exact integer arithmetic, no full-group/small-prime trap. Caveat: I refuted the specific multiform IDENTIFICATION (F4<->F5 via t<->2r same crossover); the supply face remains a legitimate but SEPARATE open object -- bounding Z_t = the zero-sum t-subset count of mu_n (a combinatorial / Sidon-type question, the #389 wall W-Johnson) -- which is NOT the BGK sqrt-cancellation wall (W-anomaly). Net effect: this connection does NOT unify the two walls; it actually SEPARATES them. No closure of the core was claimed or found.
wall: W-Johnson (the supply face = combinatorial zero-sum t-subset count of mu_n, q-independent, distinct from the W-anomaly BGK additive moment)
